source_read: PDF, pp. 259–274 (pp. 259–270 read in full, references skimmed; Table 1 and Figures 1–2 checked on rendered pages)

anchors.extracted: Evidence for brain change during abstinence comes from five small longitudinal studies: DAT PET in 5 users (Volkow et al., 2001), DAT SPECT in 5 users with 7 retested controls (Chou et al., 2007), FDG-PET in 5 users (Wang et al., 2004), FDG-PET in 10 users with 12 retested controls (Berman et al., 2007) and grey matter in 12 users with 12 retested controls (Morales et al., 2012).
anchors.note: The anchor lists four studies (5, 5, 10 and 12 users) and omits the Chou et al. (2007) SPECT study, the only DAT follow-up with retested controls (p. 265). For DAT specifically there are two studies of 5 users each.

Jaffe et al. (2005), Volkow et al. (2001) and Wang et al. (2004) had no control group retested at comparable intervals; the reviewers add that practice effects can persist for more than a year (p. 264).
6 of 7 matched studies (Leland et al., 2008, the exception); 5 of 8 statistically controlled; no well-matched study found users better on any test; most significant differences within 1 SD.

31 monozygotic and 19 dizygotic pairs; worse on Cancellation, Trail Making A, Finger Tapping and Grooved Pegboard; better on the Continuous Performance Test; no difference on the other nine tests; no urinalysis at testing.
Text: r=−0.48, p<0.01 and r=−0.42, p=0.01 (p. 267); Figure 2 prints r=−0.42, p=0.011, N=36. N is printed only for the Figure 2 correlation; the sample for r=−0.48 is not stated.

anchors.locator: Hypothesis 1, paragraphs 2–5 (p. 260, continuing on p. 261); Conclusion (p. 261)
anchors.extracted: Binge doses (2nd paragraph) and chronic moderate doses (3rd paragraph) produce cognitive deficits in rats and mice; an escalating dose beforehand largely prevented binge-induced deficits in a few rat studies (three cited); vervet monkeys given escalating doses still developed selective deficits that improved with abstinence (4th paragraph); self-administered escalating regimens also produced deficits in rats (5th paragraph; Conclusion).
anchors.note: Two corrections: the binge-dose deficits are in the 2nd paragraph, outside the stated paragraphs 3–5; the source says a few studies (three cited), not several.
